findings.claim: Two of the five step 6 rows assert a practice-stops-attack connection that the running app does not show when the practice is removed. README line 118 and the OwnBookingTest TODO ask for 'the request an attacker would send if that practice were missing', and README line 122 says the check confirms 'that its practice is what stops it'. Critic runs on the solved code, JDK 25.0.5, Maven 3.9.16, with a RANDOM_PORT probe test added in scratch: (a) validation: with the @Positive constraint removed, a non-positive booking id with a valid USER token returns 404 with the same fixed 'Booking not found' problem body as a missing booking, because the owner query already finds nothing; removing validation opens nothing here, so the row checks that the constraint is applied, not that it stops an attack. (b) safe error bodies: with ApiErrors emptied, the real servlet container answers a missing or foreign booking with Spring Boot's default error body {timestamp, status 500, error 'Internal Server Error', path} and no message, exception or trace, because spring.web.error.include-message and include-stacktrace default to 'never' and include-exception to false in Boot 4.1; the internals the row and README line 147 warn about appear only if the learner's own handler echoes the exception (the critic's echo mutant). The Boot servlet reference prose says the machine-client body includes 'the exception message', but its own property defaults and the run show it does not. (c) A smaller point on hashing: the row's 401 for the stolen stored value is produced by any one-way encoding, including the fast unsalted hashes that API2:2023 lists as vulnerable ('weakly hashed passwords'); the row shows that a copied table is not a list of working passwords (README line 143, accurate) but not why Task 1 uses bcrypt. The hashing, role and DTO rows do flip when their practice is removed (critic mutants: raw storage lets the stored value log in, a USER gets 200 on the admin endpoint, a controller returning the entity carries every field). The OWASP mappings in the after-pass block are true; the issue is the lab's demonstration for the two rows, which a learner who curls the app without the practice will see contradicted.

findings.recommendation: Keep the five rows but make the premise true for the two that are not: say for validation that the owner query would also turn the bad id away, so the constraint is defence in depth that rejects bad input at the door with a clear 400; say for safe error bodies that Spring Boot's default error body already leaves out the message, exception and trace (spring.web.error.include-*), so the practice is about the learner's own handlers never echoing exception text, which is what the row checks. Reword README line 122 and the OwnBookingTest comment to 'the practice is what answers it' for those rows, or drop the 'if that practice were missing' framing for them. Optionally add one sentence after the hashing row that a fast hash would also pass this row but is still API2's 'weakly hashed'; bcrypt keeps copied hashes slow to crack.

findings.claim: Step 6 can be passed by matching statuses to the requests the shipped tests already send, without reasoning from a practice to the risk it reduces. The hint (README line 128) says every request needed is one already seen in the lab's tests; SecurityLabTest sends only a handful of requests, and its comments pair each with the practice word or status (line 95 'the wrong role 403', line 172 'sees only the response fields', line 179 'the body reveals nothing internal', line 188 'A bad id is the client's mistake'). The row messages then name the status or caller shape each row needs ('the attacker's request must answer 403', 'send it as a logged-in caller without the ADMIN role', 'pick an action only ADMIN may take', 'the request must answer 400', 'the 400 must come from a Bean Validation constraint', 'the request must succeed (200)', 'the error must be one that your ApiErrors handler answers', 'send what the copied user table holds'), README line 193 repeats two of them outside any collapsed block, and the hashing row is forced by the helper set (one login helper and one stolen-value constant). Critic acceptance matrix, JDK 25.0.5, Maven 3.9.16: nine runs, each with one visible candidate in all five rows; every accepted candidate passed exactly its intended row. Observed: filling one visible candidate per run identified every row's request within the nine runs, and a cyclic wrong assignment (each row given another row's request) returned a message for every row that, read against the test comments, names the status or caller of the right request. Inferred, not run as a learner: a learner without a risk model can reach the passing set in two or three runs. The README after-pass block (lines 141-150) is collapsed and labelled for after the tests pass but can be opened at any time and describes three of the attacks in words. This is weaker than loop 3's copyable key (no literal answer exists and every row is decided by the running app), but the observed messages and comments give a second route to a pass that does not need the practice-to-risk reasoning #o3 names.

findings.recommendation: Either accept trial-and-match explicitly in reconciliation as a formative property of step 6, or tighten it: drop 'Every request you need is one you have already seen' from the hint; make the row messages say what the practice did with the request ('role checks did not decide this request', 'no Bean Validation constraint rejected this input') without naming the passing status or caller shape, and remove the requirement examples from README line 193; and move the after-pass block below the Done line with a plain 'read after the tests pass' instruction or into the Expected output section, so its attack descriptions are not one click from the task.

findings.claim: The hashing row's 'account that exists' depends on another test's side effect, and the OwnBookingTest TODO names callers that are not accounts. The TODO lists 'grace' and 'ada' as callers next to 'admin', but UserAccountService holds only the seeded admin account; grace exists only because task1StoresOnlyHashedPasswords registers her in the shared singleton earlier in the same cached Spring context. Critic runs on the solved code with only the hashing row changed: the stolen-value login for ada fails with 'log in as an account that exists'; the same login form for grace passes in the full mvn -q -o test run (surefire XML order under JUnit Jupiter 6.0.3: task3, task4, task1, then task7ShowsTheAttackEachPracticeStops) but fails with 'log in as an account that exists' when the same test is run alone (mvn -q -o test -Dtest=SecurityLabTest#task7ShowsTheAttackEachPracticeStops). JUnit's default method order is deterministic but intentionally nonobvious, so the full run is repeatable (lab-contract section 5 holds for the one test command) but a learner who picks the victim from the TODO's list gets a message that contradicts that list, and an answer that passes only by test-order accident.

findings.claim: Some row messages blame a correct request when the cause is elsewhere, and README line 193 overstates that rows needing earlier work 'say so'. Critic runs: (a) the solved step 6 rows on the raw starter: the hashing row correctly says Tasks 1 to 3 must be done first, but the role row says 'pick an action only ADMIN may take', the validation row 'the request must answer 400', the DTO row 'the request must succeed (200)' and the safe-errors row 'the request must end in an error', each about a correct request that failed only because Tasks 2 and 3 are not done (no chain, and the issued token is null); (b) Tasks 1-6 done with Task 7 steps 1-4 at the starter: the validation row says 'the request must answer 400' when step 3's constraint is missing, while the DTO and safe-errors rows are accurate; (c) on the finished app, the safe-errors row answers a 401 (no token) or a 403 (USER on the admin endpoint) with 'the request must end in an error', though both are error statuses; the check's own code shows why: it reads getResolvedException(), which is empty for these requests, and reports that as 'must end in an error'. Learners who do step 6 last see case (c) mostly; (a) and (b) need step 6 before earlier work.
